A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LUMINA and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Content can be reliably matched despite pagination changes and v3's added Appendix E.4.

before.justification: v1 reports original hallucination-detection experiments on RAGTruth and HalluRAG, statistical validation, ablations, and error analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds sensitivity studies, quantified error analysis, and runtime comparisons.

M1.justification: The MMD external-context score, information-processing-rate internal score, probability calibration, and combined hallucination score remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix D. The new ablations examine existing components.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate RAGTruth's question answering, summarization, and data-to-text tasks and HalluRAG's answerable questions. Retrieval-noise and proxy-generator scenarios are retained. New analyses use the existing data; additional detector backbones change model settings.

E2.justification: Detection comparators in Tables 2–4 remain unchanged, including ReDeEP and SAPLMA. v3 newly evaluates ReDeEP as a runtime comparator in Table 7; v1's computational-resources section reports only LUMINA's runtime.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 replaces the Qwen2.5-7B detector with Qwen3-4B and Llama4-17B. Added protocols include top-k and component controls, GPT-5 classification of 50 false positives and 50 false negatives, and comparative timing. Core benchmark splits, metrics, and default settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained noise, kernel, signal-combination, and lambda studies, Appendix E.4 adds tests of MMD approximation size, random-document selection, and the separate layer-weighting and entropy-normalization components. Appendix F extends qualitative error inspection with a quantified 100-case analysis, substantially deepening design validation and failure analysis.

E5.justification: Appendix E.4 newly reports five rounds using different random documents and a standard deviation below 0.0025. This is a focused addition of variability reporting; Table 1's hypothesis tests and significance-reporting practice remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their values, but v3 adds substantial supplementary results: component-ablation AUROCs, sensitivity findings, error proportions, runtimes, and replacement proxy-detector results. Table 6 attributes 64% of sampled false negatives to summarization-related low scores; Table 7 reports 0.69 versus 0.86 seconds/sample for LUMINA versus ReDeEP with Llama2-7B.

T1.justification: Conjecture 1, the mathematical definitions, derivations, and hypotheses H1–H4 remain unchanged. Equation 11 drops the superscript 1 from R without changing the defined quantity. Added motivation around the conjecture supplies intuition rather than new formal assumptions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: context–knowledge-based detection, statistical score validation, strong benchmark performance, and robustness to retrieval noise and proxy detection. The additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v3 clarifies the motivation for tasks requiring external information and adds discussion of reasoning-intensive failures when the two scores are close, recommending task-dependent weighting. Appendix G also explains the runtime advantage through attention-map storage and logit-lens costs. Existing summarization and retrieval-quality limitations remain.

D1.justification: The anonymous code reference is replaced by a named GitHub repository reference, also displayed beneath the abstract. Appendix G adds model-specific runtime information and computational-cost explanations. The top-100 approximation, score calibration, and single-H100 hardware disclosure already appeared in v1.

R1.justification: The Qwen2.5 reference is removed and Qwen3 and Llama4 references are added for the revised detector selection. Park et al. (2025) is no longer attributed the two assumptions in Section 4.3. The principal related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: v3 expands the conjecture's motivation, reorders the ablation discussion, adds Appendix E.4, and makes limited grammatical, author-name, and publication-header edits. It also reconciles the appendix's manual-error count with the main text's 20 cases per class. Most prose and organization are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 5–7 and revises Figure 3's detector rows and axes. The existing kernel and signal-combination plots exchange figure numbers and placement, while Table 2 receives spacing adjustments. Most figures, table structures, and visual styling remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added component and sensitivity studies strengthen support for existing design choices, while quantified errors and comparative runtimes improve practical assessment. These are useful incremental gains with the method and headline results unchanged. Their value is limited by sparse procedural detail for GPT-5 error classification and timing, plus Table 7's unexplained 'Llama2-17B' label.
